native.answer:
Finding support groups can be really helpful during a time like this. While I don't have a constantly updated directory, I know of several organizations that *often* have resources and connections to support groups, and are good places to start looking for something specifically geared towards young adults with Hodgkin lymphoma undergoing bone marrow transplants.

Here are a few:

*   **The Leukemia & Lymphoma Society (LLS):** They have a lot of information about Hodgkin lymphoma and often list support groups, both in-person and online. They may have specific programs for young adults. [https://www.lls.org/](https://www.lls.org/)
*   **Cancer Research UK:** While UK-based, they have excellent resources and may list international support groups or online forums. [https://www.cancerresearchuk.org/](https://www.cancerresearchuk.org/)
*   **The Bone Marrow & Leukemia Trust:** This organization focuses specifically on bone marrow transplants and related blood cancers. [https://www.leukaemiatrust.org/](https://www.leukaemiatrust.org/)
*   **Young Adult Cancer Canada (if you are in Canada):** They focus specifically on the needs of young adults with cancer. [https://www.youngadultcancer.ca/](https://www.youngadultcancer.ca/)
*   **Imerman Angels:** This is a one-on-one mentoring program where she could be paired with someone who has been through a similar experience. [https://www.imermanangels.org/](https://www.imermanangels.org/)

Additionally, many hospitals with bone marrow transplant centers have their own support groups or can connect her with local resources. Her transplant team is a great place to ask.

It's also worth searching online for "young adult Hodgkin lymphoma bone marrow transplant support group" – but be cautious about the source and ensure it's a reputable organization.
